resolved_findings.resolution: reorder() now bulk-sets service_order=NULL for the whole locked checked-in cohort (UPDATE ... WHERE id=ANY($1::uuid[])) before assigning final contiguous 1..length values, structurally removing every touched row from the partial unique index before any new value is written -- eliminating the gap-collision case entirely rather than relying on a safe offset. Also wraps the update in a try/catch translating 23505 to QueueConflictError as defense in depth. Independently re-verified: re-ran the original real-Postgres repro (check in 3, no_show the middle one, check in a 4th, reorder the first entry to the back) against this exact head in a fresh worktree -- it now succeeds with deterministic service_order [1,2,3], where it previously threw a raw 23505. Full existing suite (lifecycle/clinic-scheduling/walk-in/database/unit/API, typecheck, lint) also re-run clean. Note: GitHub CI had not actually run for this exact head at review time (author-confirmed empty check rollup); this resolution rests on independent local verification, not a CI badge.
